simple.meaning: מַטֶּה (maṭṭeh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a branch (as extending ); figuratively, a tribe ; also a rod , whether for chastising (figuratively, correction ), ruling (a sceptre ), throwing (a lance ), or walking (a staff ; figuratively, a support of life, e.g. bread).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 252 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, beginning at Genesis 38:18. Its contexts include family, family line, Torah, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַטֶּה (H4294).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַטֶּה (maṭṭeh) / H4294 is traced through Genesis 38:18, Genesis 38:25, Exodus 4:2, Exodus 4:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

Moses said to the children of Israel, “Behold, Yahweh has called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has put in his heart that he may teach, both he and Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.
Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that Yahweh commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, and a skillful workman, and an embroiderer in blue, in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name, and cursed; and they brought him to Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
When I break your staff of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall deliver your bread again by weight. You shall eat, and not be satisfied.
With you there shall be a man of every tribe, each one head of his fathers’ house.
